newsitem.title: UK: Shippers want intergrated freighters - Burlington PZ.
newsitem.headline: Shippers want intergrated freighters - Burlington PZ.

text.p: Shippers are no longer prepared to deal with a multitude of service providers in a fast changing industry, said Burlington Air Express, vice president Steve Finch.
Instead they want a single unit that can satisfy all their transport and logistics needs especially as major firms increasingly focus on core activities and outsource non-core ones.

This offers the freight industry an opportunity to offer new value added services such as inventory control, repair and return centres, kit building, order processing. product assembly and parts/material procurement, Finch told SMi's Competitiveness and Profitability in Air Cargo Conference.
Modern business demands the efficiencies that will occur when the customer moves towards a "full service provider" rather than being offered different services by different firms.

The development of a traditional forwarder into a logistics provider now requires a global network of offices equipped with information technology and Finch warned that firms not making these changes "will simply not survive into the next millennium."

Shippers want freight firms to offer a full range of services covering air, ocean, road trasport, express shipmenmt and warehousing distribution all operating from a global network of offices, Finch stated.
A global network is important for firms aiming to remain competitive by global sourcing from an increasing number of manufacturing bases in low cost third world countries, Finch stated.
